In the context of TikTok, there has been a significant rise in birdwatching videos due to their popularity among younger demographics. This aligns with how users engage with content on these platforms.

YouTube recently updated its view-counting system to match the approach used by other social media platforms like Instagram and TikTok, which adds a view as soon as a video starts playing. This change in view counting could further boost the numbers for creators whose videos are viewed more frequently.

The shift towards engaging younger audiences on social media is also evident with No 10 hiring a TikTok team member to understand and engage with this demographic. As traditional routes into journalism become less viable, businesses are increasingly turning to content creators like those found in TikTok to reach their target audience effectively.

Regarding birding apps, they fit into the trend by offering users information about birds which makes it easier for them to identify species from videos or images shared on platforms like TikTok. Apps provide a supplementary tool that complements the visual and auditory aspects of birdwatching content.
